task.title: Relics: merge body edits automatically
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

Today two edits to the same body are always a conflict, even when they touch different lines. This story merges them automatically where that is safe, and gives the agent a clear report when it is not.

## How it works, by example

1. Alice and Bob both read the Goals part at version `c1`.
2. Alice saves new text, saying she started from `c1`. It goes in as change `c2`.
3. Bob saves his text, also saying he started from `c1`. The current version is `c2`, so Workbook knows Bob never saw Alice's text.
4. Workbook compares three texts: `c1` (where both started), `c2` (Alice's) and Bob's.
   - If they changed different lines, the combined text is saved as `c3`, recorded as a merge of the two.
   - If they changed the same lines, Bob gets a conflict that shows all three texts.

## Rules that matter

- The merge is line by line. Git's own three-way file merge is the expected method.
- The merge runs once, on the clone that syncs second, and its result is stored as its own change with its own version. Other clones read the stored result and never re-run the merge, so the method can improve later without changing old relics.
- History records that a merge happened and the three versions that went into it.
- Workbook never stores conflict markers or a half-merged value.
- A body whose format is not text, or whose starting version was compacted away, is a conflict and is never merged.
- The same applies when the command itself is given an out-of-date starting version: it merges or reports, and never replaces newer text.
- There is no overwrite option.
- The stored-history check from the first relic story still holds: a body edit counts only if the version it started from was current at that point, and a merged text is a separate change that names its inputs.

## The conflict report

- The command stops with the existing conflict exit code and returns the starting text, the local text and the other text, in text and in `--json`.
- The agent resolves the conflict when the intent is clear and saves again from the current version. Otherwise it shows the user both versions and asks.
- The documentation and the Workbook skill lay this flow out clearly, with an example.

## Done when

- Two clones editing different lines of one body both keep their work with no report.
- Two clones editing the same lines get a conflict with three texts, and nothing half-merged is stored.
- A third clone that syncs later reads the stored merge and computes nothing.
- The same history gives the same text on every clone, whatever order it arrives in.
- History and `relic diff` show a merge as a merge.

## Not in this story

Merging task descriptions, which is the next story.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
